newsitem.title: USA: LA County area to spend $46 mln on pollution probe.
newsitem.headline: LA County area to spend $46 mln on pollution probe.

text.p: A Los Angeles County Sanitation District and 155 other municipal governments in the area agreed to pay $45.7 million to investigate pollution off the coast of Los Angeles, the Justice Department said Tuesday.
Under the settlement, the local governments must restore fish and wildife populations damaged by PCBs and the "largest-ever deposit" of DDT in U.S. coastal waters, the department said.

The settlement stems from a Superfund toxic waste cleanup case brought by the U.S. government in 1990 alleging that Montrose Chemical Corp, which owned a DDT plant in Los Angeles County, had released toxic substances into the environment.
Los Angeles County Sanitation District 2 will pay $21.86 million to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and $140,000 to the state to help clean up the contamination.
The municipalities will pay $23 million in damages to federal and state trustees for natural resources that were harmed by DDT and PCB.
